items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: And that’s how we became so friendly with Dorothy and Dick.

ctx.x: Oh, that’s great. How did you get into the radio production business?

Let’s see what happened? Well I needed a job and my husband, Bob Bach, was producing “What’s My Line.” He thought it up, little knowing it was going to take off and be a 27 year run. And that’s how we became so friendly with Dorothy and Dick. So he came home one day and he said, “gee we’re thinking of reviving ‘Luncheon at Sardi’s’ which was a terrible program,” and he said, “Arlene said they came to her,” Arlene Francis, and he said, “she needs someone to produce it, do you want to do it?” So I wasn’t doing…

you and I said, “here are the things” I thought that she’d just give me a — like when you get weighed and they give you a ticket and it say “you will travel” you know, the little wing see? But before they could figure out what I should do I got this job. And it was marvelous. Because I didn’t do much about jazz, Arlene was not too musical. But I was interesting in overthrowing the government at the time so that was my platform. Arlene was willing to go along with anything. One day she said, “you’re my puppet.” No…
